questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

The diagram shows a production possibility curve (LM) for an economy producing agricultural goods and manufacturing goods. L agricultural goods R T S M O manufacturing goods What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: The economy must be allocatively efficient at point R.
options.B: The economy is Pareto efficient at point T.
options.C: The economy is productively efficient at point S.
options.D: The opportunity cost is constant as we move from L to M.

questions.questionText: The private benefit of an activity is greater than the private cost. The social benefit of the same activity is less than the social cost. What must be true of the activity?

options.A: external benefit = external cost
options.B: external benefit > external cost
options.C: external benefit < external cost
options.D: external benefit > private benefit

questions.questionText: What is the central principle of marginal utility theory?

options.A: As more is consumed of a normal good, the additional satisfaction gained increases.
options.B: Consumers are in equilibrium when the marginal utility gained from good X equals the price of good Y.
options.C: Consumers are in equilibrium when the ratio of the marginal utility of goods X and Y are equal to the ratio of their prices.
options.D: Consumers are in equilibrium when the total utility gained from good X is the same as gained from good Y.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows five budget lines. Line 1 is the original budget line. food O drink Which pair of budget lines shows a relatively higher price for drink compared with food after a move from budget line 1?

options.A: 2 and 3 B 2 and 4 C 3 and 5 D 4 and 5

questions.questionText: Broken rice is an inferior good. What would be the resulting income and substitution effect on the quantity demanded of broken rice if its price falls? quantity demanded quantity demanded due to income due to substitution effect effect

options.A: falls falls
options.B: falls rises
options.C: rises falls
options.D: rises rises

questions.questionText: Firms in a market decide to collude over the price that they charge for their products. What is not likely to be a feature of the market?

options.A: Firms have similar cost structures.
options.B: Products of the firms are close substitutes.
options.C: There are high barriers to entry into the market.
options.D: There is a large number of competing firms.

questions.questionText: Firms often remain small even when growth could result in technical economies of scale. What is not a likely reason for this?

options.A: Demand for the product tends to change often and rapidly.
options.B: Individual entrepreneurs wish to keep a tight personal control over their own firm.
options.C: The entrepreneurs who establish the firms tend to be ambitious risk-takers.
options.D: The market in which they operate is very specialised in nature, often selling unique products.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the short-run equilibrium for a firm operating in a monopolistically competitive market. cost, revenue AC MC P AR MR O Q
In which circumstance would direct provision of a product by the government be least likely?

options.A: when fixed costs are very high
options.B: when the demand for the product is very high but unit costs are low
options.C: when the industry faces large natural barriers to entry
options.D: when the minimum efficient scale of production is above the level of demand at current prices

questions.questionText: The table shows a firm’s total costs corresponding to different levels of output. units of output 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 total cost ($) 8 14 18 22 28 36 46 58 If the market price is $8, within which range of output would a profit-maximising firm in a perfectly competitive industry produce in the short run?

options.A: 1–2 units B 3–4 units C 5–6 units D 7–8 units

questions.questionText: What would encourage an increase in the number of small firms?

options.A: increasing government regulation of conditions in the workplace
options.B: more risk-averse (cautious) lending policies by banks
options.C: stronger government laws against the growth of monopoly
options.D: tougher penalties in the case of personal bankruptcy

questions.questionText: What is not a source of market failure?

options.A: imperfect information
options.B: income inequality
options.C: monopoly
options.D: non-excludability

questions.questionText: A government issues free non-tradeable pollution permits to firms. They specify the maximum amount of polluting gases these firms are allowed to emit. In a change in legislation, the permits can be traded with other firms. Assuming that all other costs and revenues remain the same, what will be the impact on the profits of the firms that are now buyers or sellers of the permits? profits of buyers profits of sellers of permits of permits

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: What is an example of ‘nudge’ theory when applied to encouraging healthy eating?

options.A: advertising the benefits of healthy eating
options.B: increasing tax on sugary foods
options.C: introducing a subsidy for fruit growers
options.D: supermarkets putting fruit near cash registers

questions.questionText: What is a definition of transfer earnings?

options.A: the amount of earnings above that needed to keep a worker in their current job
options.B: the minimum earnings needed to keep a worker in their current job
options.C: the social security benefits paid to workers whose earnings are below the poverty line
options.D: the amount of earnings needed to cause a worker to change to a different job

questions.questionText: The chart gives information about the average daily wage rate for all industries in India. rupees 270 per day 2011 2012 2013 2014 year What could have caused this trend in wage rates?

options.A: an increase in capital-intensive production
options.B: an increase in the number of industrial workers
options.C: an increase in the number of people unemployed
options.D: an increase in the productivity of labour

questions.questionText: The table shows the annual percentage economic growth rates of three countries from 2012 to 2018. annual percentage change in real GDP Brazil % Japan % Spain % 2012 1.9 1.5 –2.9 2013 3.0 2.0 –1.7 2014 0.5 0.4 1.4 2015 –3.5 1.2 3.7 2016 –3.3 0.6 3.2 2017 1.1 1.9 3.0 2018 1.1 0.8 2.6 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Brazil was in the downturn of its trade cycle in 2015.
options.B: Japan’s real GDP was at its smallest in 2014.
options.C: Spain experienced the worst recession of the period.
options.D: Spain was in the downturn of its trade cycle in 2014.

questions.questionText: What could cause the official statistics for the national income per head of a developing country to overstate the true level of economic well-being of its inhabitants?

options.A: if there is dependence on barter in internal trade
options.B: if subsistence agriculture dominates total economic activity
options.C: if services are an important component of exports
options.D: if there is extreme income inequality

questions.questionText: What is shown by the Kuznets curve?

options.A: the rise and then fall in the balance of trade deficit following a devaluation
options.B: the rise and then fall in the economic growth rate as the GDP increases
options.C: the rise and then fall in inequality as the level of income per head rises
options.D: the rise and then fall in tax revenue as the tax rate is increased

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment is associated with a deficiency in aggregate demand?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: structural
options.D: voluntary

questions.questionText: There has been a switch in demand from goods produced by labour-intensive methods of production to similar goods produced using high-technology methods of production. This has led to an overall increase in unemployment. What is the best policy to reduce this type of unemployment?

options.A: reduce the rate of income tax
options.B: increase the rate of interest on borrowing for investment
options.C: subsidise products produced by labour-intensive methods
options.D: subsidise exports produced by high-technology industries

questions.questionText: What would not exist in a free-market, open economy?

options.A: autonomous investment
options.B: household saving
options.C: import spending
options.D: indirect taxation

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be found in an economy with a positive output gap?

options.A: a higher potential than actual GDP
options.B: high unemployment
options.C: inflation
options.D: low labour costs

questions.questionText: Which statement about the Keynesian liquidity preference demand for money model is correct?

options.A: Both the transactions and precautionary motives for holding liquidity are interest rate elastic.
options.B: The demand for liquidity is completely interest rate inelastic at low rates of interest.
options.C: The demand to hold liquidity by households is stable.
options.D: The rate of interest on long-term government securities is inversely related to their price.

questions.questionText: The table shows an individual’s planned consumption at different levels of income. income ($) 100 200 300 400 500 consumption ($) 140 220 300 380 460 What can be concluded about changes in the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) and average propensities to consume (APC) as income rises? MPC APC

options.A: constant constant
options.B: constant falling
options.C: falling constant
options.D: falling falling

questions.questionText: Which items in the table are classified as foreign aid? official portfolio foreign direct development investment investment assistance flows

options.A: no no yes
options.B: no yes no
options.C: yes no yes
options.D: yes yes no

questions.questionText: An increase in which factor will cause a decrease in investment spending?

options.A: business confidence
options.B: company profits
options.C: interest rates
options.D: national income

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between tax revenue and the tax rate. tax revenue collected 0 25 50 75 100 tax rate on income (%) What is the curve on the diagram called?

options.A: income elasticity curve
options.B: J curve
options.C: Lorenz curve
options.D: Laffer curve

questions.questionText: The table shows the rate of inflation (consumer prices index) and the monthly percentage rate of unemployment for the USA over a six month period in 2017. month April May June July Aug Sept rate of inflation (%) 2.2 1.9 1.6 1.7 1.9 2.2 rate of unemployment (%) 3.9 3.8 3.9 3.9 3.8 3.7 What can be concluded from this table?

options.A: Falling inflation leads to lower unemployment.
options.B: Increasing inflation leads to rising unemployment.
options.C: The rate of inflation correlates exactly with the rate of unemployment.
